        How the score is calculated

        The score is computed from what ARGUS-1's checks last observed, grouped into protection areas. Each area loses points for its open findings, and critical and high findings cost far more than medium ones. Low-severity items are inventory, not risk, so they do not lower it.

        A check that is failing, stale or has never run is not counted as safe. It is shown as unverified and pulls the score down in proportion to how much of the computer is unobserved. A finding you have marked as expected is counted as low, with a reason and an expiry.

        The score reflects what ARGUS-1 could check. A low score is not proof of an attack and a high score is not proof of safety.

        Words used in ARGUS-1
        Collector
        One of ARGUS-1's checks. Each looks at one area, such as startup items or the firewall, and reports what it found.
        Stale data
        A check's last result is too old to trust. It is not counted as checked.
        Persistence
        A way for a program to start again after a restart, such as a scheduled task. Normal software uses it, and so does malware.
        Firewall rule
        A setting that allows or blocks network connections for a program or port.
        Unsigned program
        A program without a publisher's digital signature. Many developer tools are unsigned, so it is a reason to look, not proof of harm.
        Credential exposure
        A password or key stored where others might read it. It matters if the credential is real and still active.
        Coverage
        How much of the computer ARGUS-1's checks are currently able to see.

        Settings

        Setup, alerts and what stays on this computer. Appearance and notifications are in the top bar.

        Privacy and data

        The dashboard is served only on this computer's own address (127.0.0.1). It loads nothing from other websites.

        The assistant's local model is only contacted on this computer; other addresses are refused. If it is not running, the assistant still answers from ARGUS-1's own data.

        Secret-looking values such as keys, tokens and passwords are masked wherever findings are shown here.

        Detail level and notifications

        Simple shows plain language first and keeps technical evidence one click away. Advanced opens the technical sections and shows identifiers. It is one interface with two depths, and the choice is remembered in this browser only.

        Notifications are listed in the bell in the top bar: new serious findings, monitoring problems, proposals that need your approval, investigation updates and action results. An unchanged finding is announced once. They are in-app only. The Notify me button adds pop-ups for new critical findings, and those work only while this page is open: ARGUS-1 has no background notifier.

        Anything that could change something is shown in a confirmation first, with the risk, whether it can be undone and what happens if you do nothing. Closing it, pressing Escape, or letting it expire changes nothing.
